key_insight: Three joint-embedding predictive formulations trained stably without representational collapse but consistently underperformed standard masked language modelling for longitudinal EHR representation learning.
clinical_relevance: These findings caution against assuming that stable latent-space prediction yields better patient representations for downstream clinical tasks.
method: Adapted three Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) formulations to longitudinal EHR sequences.
Compared latent-space prediction with masked language modelling (MLM).
Examined how target size and heterogeneity affect prediction error.
evidence_signal: Experiments on MIMIC-IV found that target size, rather than heterogeneity, increased prediction error, while smaller targets did not recover downstream performance.
watch_item: The abstract reports evidence from one dataset without task-specific metrics, limiting assessment of performance gaps and generalisability.
paper_title: Are Joint-Embedding Predictive Objectives Effective for Longitudinal EHRs?
